title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a synthetic depiction of real people published as documentary imagery. A photograph of three students at a Stanford event was altered with artificial intelligence so that one student, Billy Ramirez, was replaced by a different person and the others were made to look thinner, and the result ran on Stanford banners as an image of that event. The failure sits at the point where an institutional communications asset is produced and released, not inside a model's output alone. The banner presented a fabricated scene as a record of something that happened.

Stanford's own policy bans using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements, and the university said both the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Catching this required a review step before publication that compared the altered image against the policy and confirmed whether disclosure was needed. Stanford has said it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises on training and on making sure materials are properly reviewed, which is the check that was absent.

It is not established which AI tool was used, who performed the alteration, or whether anyone intended to violate the policy, and a reported policy violation is not a finding of intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic Stanford senior majoring in human biology, was in a 2024 Lunar New Year photo with two other students. Stanford's dining service posted it online the next day. When Stanford used the image on banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by a Black woman, and the other students were altered to look thinner. Ramirez learned about it from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated, though he also saw a comedic element.

Stanford said on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to change the original image. The university said its policy strictly bans using A.I. to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said both the alteration and the failure to disclose it violated that policy. Stanford is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to add training and make sure all materials are properly reviewed.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
